items: A 3,000-year-old burial ground of a seafaring people called the Lapita has been found on an abandoned <input> on the Pacific island of Éfaté. The cemetery, which is a significant <input>, was uncovered accidentally by an agricultural worker.
The Lapita explored and colonised many Pacific islands over several centuries. They took many things with them on their voyages including <input> and tools.

The burial ground increases the amount of information about the Lapita available to scientists. A team of researchers, led by Matthew Spriggs from the Australian National University, are helping with the excavation of the site. Spriggs believes the <input> which was found at the site is very important since it confirms that the <input> found inside are Lapita.
